title: Overridden method execution during construction
answer: If a superclass constructor calls an overridable instance method, normal dynamic dispatch can invoke the subclass override even before the subclass constructor body and field initializers have completed. Therefore the subclass method executes, but it may observe default values for subclass state. This is a major reason to avoid overridable method calls from constructors; construction should not expose partially initialized objects to subclass behavior.
